title: Rhode Island Holiday Guide
intro: Holiday shows, concerts, lights, Santa, markets and church bazaars across Rhode Island, from early November through New Year’s Day, with times, places and prices.

items.note: Trinity Rep’s 50th-anniversary production of its holiday classic.

items.t: 'Twas the Night Before... by Cirque du Soleil
items.note: Cirque du Soleil’s holiday family show: acrobatics, dance, characters and Christmas music.
items.more: Shows: Nov 24 and 25 at 7; Nov 27 at 4 and 7:30; Nov 28 at 1, 4 and 7:30; Nov 29 at noon, 3 and 6:30; Dec 2 at 7; Dec 3 and 4 at 7:30; Dec 5 at 1, 4 and 7:30; Dec 6 at noon and 3. PPAC has a family-ticket offer.

items.t: Sara Evans: Holiday Road Tour with Braden Hull
items.where: The Historic Park Theatre & Event Center
items.note: Sara Evans brings her holiday tour to Cranston.

items.t: Vienna Boys Choir: Christmas in Vienna
items.where: The Historic Park Theatre & Event Center
items.note: The Vienna Boys Choir performs its Christmas program.

items.t: Boston Pops Holiday Concert with Keith Lockhart
items.note: Keith Lockhart leads “Sleigh Ride,” seasonal arrangements, a sing-along and a visit from Santa. The afternoon show was added after the evening sold well.

items.where: The Historic Park Theatre & Event Center
items.note: Irish music and dance celebrate Christmas traditions.
Clara’s Christmas Eve story with Tchaikovsky’s score, Ballet RI dancers and local young performers. Some matinees offer a post-show “Meet the Stars.”
items.more: Shows: Dec 17 and 18 at 7; Dec 19 and 20 at 1 and 6:30; Dec 23 at 6:30; Dec 26 at 1 and 6:30; Dec 27 at 1.

items.t: Disney On Ice: Magic in the Stars
items.note: Frozen 2, Moana, Encanto, Toy Story and more on ice, with no Christmas Day show.
Newport Contemporary Ballet’s Nutcracker moves through Rosecliff’s rooms, with a Newport-themed second act.
items.more: Opens Nov 25 at 5:30; then two shows a day Nov 27–29 and Dec 1–4. Ages 6 and up.

items.note: The Arctic Playhouse stages Dickens’s story of Ebenezer Scrooge and the supernatural visitors who force him to reconsider his life.
The unruly Herdmans transform a Christmas pageant.
Scrooge rediscovers compassion through ghostly encounters.
The Stadium Theatre’s adaptation of A Christmas Carol follows Ebenezer Scrooge through the visits that challenge his isolation and reshape his understanding of Christmas.
Beloved carols and contemporary choral works, presented by Newport Classical.
Handel’s Messiah in the Rosecliff ballroom, sung by Ensemble Altera and the Professional Choristers of the Choir School of Newport County.
The Providence College Chorus and Liturgical Choir, followed by hot chocolate and cookies.

items.t: Ocean State Pops Orchestra: Holiday Pops
items.note: The orchestra presents a holiday pops concert.

items.t: The Irish Tenors: A Family Christmas
items.note: The Irish Tenors bring their family Christmas show to Washington Square.
Music from The Nutcracker, Vivaldi’s Winter, “Carol of the Bells” and a Christmas sing-along.

items.t: Westerly Band Holiday Concert: Tribute to America and the Holidays
items.note: A holiday and patriotic concert by the Westerly Band, America’s oldest active community band. A family event.
items.price: $8 suggested donation for adults; children free
items.more: Doors open at 1 p.m.

items.note: The Rhode Island Philharmonic and the Providence Singers, conducted by Christine Noel, in a Sunday matinee of Handel’s Messiah.
items.addr: The VETS, 1 Avenue of the Arts, Providence

items.where: Cathedral of Saints Peter and Paul
items.note: The Gregorian Concert Choir and Festival Orchestra perform Advent and Christmas music. Proceeds go to the Diocese of Providence’s Keep the Heat On program.

items.t: Very Merry Dickens Carolers at Island Cemetery and Belmont Chapel
items.note: A seasonal caroling appearance; the listing does not give a time.

items.t: A Musical Retelling of ‘A Christmas Carol’ with Christine Baranski
items.note: One night only: the vocal ensemble Skylark sings the story, narrated by actress Christine Baranski.
Holiday favorites, old and new.

items.t: A Christmas Carol, read by Michael Langlois
items.note: A theatrical reading of Dickens’s story in the mansion’s dining room.
A half-mile path of holiday lights at The Breakers, with a look inside the decorated mansion on the same timed ticket.
The Bristol mansion decorated for Christmas, with the evening Sparkle! light display on the grounds.
items.more: Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas.

items.note: Light displays, a makers village, seasonal food and drink, entertainment and Santa visits.
Decorated boats circle the harbor competing for best display.
items.more: Good views from Perrotti Park, Bowen’s Wharf and Bannister’s Wharf.

items.note: Free synchronized light show you watch from your car; tune to 106.9 FM. Donations support The Autism Project.
Community activities, a project benefiting Adoption Rhode Island, samples, and Santa arriving in a vintage car around 4:30.
items.more: Part of Garden City’s Holiday Happenings, with Santa’s Cabin and Letters to Santa through the season.

items.note: Tree lighting with Santa, photos, children’s crafts, letters to Santa and music.
items.more: Rain date Nov 29.

items.note: Carolers, seasonal decorations, hot chocolate for the children and cider as the Goat Island lighthouse lights up.
Explore illuminated holiday displays.
Tree lighting at Updike Park Thursday; Santa arrives by boat at the Town Dock on selected afternoons, with carols and hayrides; Elf Parade Saturday. Some shops open until 9 p.m. Friday and Saturday.
The campus glows with 1,000 luminarias.
Richmond’s yearly tree lighting on the Town Hall green. Last year Santa and Mrs. Claus arrived by sleigh, the elementary school choir sang, and fire pits lined the grounds.
items.more: Check the town for this year’s time.

items.note: The garden trails become a winter wonderland of decorated trees, with children’s activities, caroling, music, cocoa and handmade local gifts.
items.more: Last season it was open 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. on most Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, and children’s tickets were $8. Check the garden for this year’s days.

items.t: Coventry Winter Wonderland Craft Fair and Tree Lighting
items.note: The 4th annual fair: craft vendors, food trucks, Santa photos at no charge and family activities from 10 to 5, then the town tree lighting from 5:30 to 6:30.
items.more: Rain date Dec 6.

items.note: The 56th annual lighting: Santa and live music from about 12:30, local musicians and choruses through the afternoon, and the tree lighting at 6 p.m. Santa and Mrs. Claus arrive by boat, weather permitting.

Decorated trees, a miniature village, a talking snowman, carousel and train rides, horse-drawn hayrides, Santa, face painting and children’s crafts. Opening night has the mayor’s tree lighting, with Santa arriving by fire truck.
Community choirs, Santa’s parade into downtown, live bands, family activities, food trucks and an ice-skating DJ party.
Holiday fires illuminate the basin, with onshore programming beginning at 4 PM.
Decorated trees glow along the walkway.
A three-hour outing with a train ride, the story, hot chocolate and Santa.

items.t: Seasonal skating at The Providence Rink
items.note: Listed as open daily during the festival season. Check the rink calendar for hours, tickets and bumper-car sessions.

items.t: Ice Theatre of New York at The Providence Rink
items.note: Ice-dance performances, followed by a public skating dance party with a DJ.

items.t: Santa and Mrs. Claus Arrive by Boat
items.note: Welcome Santa and Mrs. Claus at the wharf before their fire-truck ride to the Conanicut Gift Shop.
Photos with Mr. and Mrs. Claus, with cookies and cocoa, at the seaside inn.
items.more: Last year it began at 2 p.m. Check the inn for this year’s time.

items.note: Families visit Santa in a sensory-friendly setting.
A family holiday tea includes a special guest and photos; a waitlist is available.
Participants build and decorate a gingerbread animal exhibit.
Carol singing and a Christmas reading accompany Santa's visit.
About an hour on a decorated boat with Santa, hot chocolate and holiday music.
items.more: Sailings: Dec 14 at 2; Dec 19 at 11; Dec 20 at 11 and 1; Dec 21, 22 and 23 at 11. Book: 401-423-9900.

items.t: Christmas Pageant at St. Francis Church
items.note: The children’s Christmas pageant, after the 9 a.m. Mass.
A hands-on Winter Wonder Workshop to make a snowman ornament.

items.t: Garden City Center Holiday Farmers Market
items.note: Holiday pop-up market presented with Rhode Island Night Market. Check the listing for daily hours and vendors.

items.t: Holiday Sip & Shop at Mount Hope Farm
items.note: An evening of holiday shopping at the farm.
The Bristol Merchants Association’s yearly preview night: shops stay open late. Follow the luminaries to the stores taking part.

items.time: Sat 10 AM–4 PM; Sun 11 AM–3 PM
items.note: More than 150 vendors, entertainment and food trucks at an indoor family holiday festival.
Author Lisa Goddard signs her children’s holiday book.
Nearly 100 independent makers under one roof for holiday shopping, about half from Rhode Island.
items.more: Free parking on site. Wheelchair accessible.

items.note: The Breakers, Marble House and Chateau-sur-Mer decorated with Christmas trees, wreaths, flowers and period table settings.

items.t: Christmas Preparations with the 1910 Household Staff
items.note: Costumed household staff show how the manor got ready for a 1910 Christmas, then you tour the decorated house on your own.
items.more: Two timed sessions; check Blithewold for tickets.

items.note: A visit with Santa, co-hosted with Lorelei’s for Littles.
items.more: Time not listed; check before you go.

items.note: Seasonal workshop led by the mansion's private-events manager.
Check Blithewold's booking page for available dates and seats.

items.t: A Rough Point Holiday: After Dark
items.note: Doris Duke’s oceanfront house decorated for the season and open after dark, with warm drinks and jazz.

items.t: Holiday Jazz Tea with Chelley Knight’s Quartet
items.note: Live jazz with afternoon tea in the manor dining room.
items.more: Rain date Nov 29.

items.note: A German-style Christmas market with more than 25 artisans: pottery, ornaments, soaps, jewelry, textiles, wreaths, holiday greens and German food.
The Rhode Island Shriners’ fundraiser: decorated trees, wreaths and menorahs raffled off, a craft and vendor fair, Santa visits and a Candy Land kids’ area.
items.more: Free parking; accessible. Check the venue for hours.

items.note: A holiday brunch with Santa on Goat Island.
A seasonal decorating competition. Discover Newport is inviting participation for the 2026 program.
Sidewalks lined with luminaria, hayrides with Santa, strolling carolers, and hot chocolate and a cookie while you shop downtown Westerly-Pawcatuck.
Make a holiday wreath with Blithewold’s horticulture team.
items.more: Check Blithewold for supplies and price.

items.note: Thursdays Dec 3, 10 and 17: village shopping, Santa photos and open-mic Christmas caroling. Dec 3 adds the tree lighting at Kent Field at 6, crafts at Manton Library and dinner at Chepachet Union Church.

items.time: Thu–Fri 5–9 PM; Sat noon–8; Sun noon–5
items.note: Local makers, food, seasonal activities and pop-up entertainment.
items.addr: Grant’s Block Park and Westminster St., Providence

items.t: Wreath Decorating Workshop at Mount Hope Farm
items.note: An evening wreath-decorating workshop in the farm’s barn.
items.more: Confirm price and registration with the farm.

items.where: Pawtucket Armory Center for the Arts
items.note: Artists sell handmade holiday gifts.
The weekend brings together the Downcity market, tree lighting, skating, workshops, entertainment and trolley service. Check the festival site for lineup updates.
A multi-faith gathering with music, dance and prayers reflecting traditions of light and themes of mercy and care for the Earth.
Holiday shopping inside the historic Colony House.

items.where: Biltmore Park and Providence Rink to Grant's Block
items.note: A lighted procession led by the Providence Drum Troupe and pop-up performers, heading to the Downcity Holiday Market.
An advance shopping evening before the main market.
A holiday evening at the historic house, catered by Russell Morin. Check the organizer for admission and age requirements.
Village shops and craft fairs celebrate the season, with Santa arriving by boat at 1 PM.
Make a fresh wreath with the Preservation Society’s greenhouse staff.
Live music, dance and festive lighting animate Federal Hill.

items.t: Bristol Christmas Festival and European Market
items.note: Vendor huts, holiday food, crafts, stage and street entertainment, Santa, wreath decorating and children’s crafts.
Town tree lighting at the Burnside Building, Hope and Court streets, with local school performers.
items.more: Rain date Dec 6.

items.note: Indoor market with local makers, food trucks, music, children’s activities and Santa.
Holiday shopping from local makers.
Colonial decorations, live music, traditional wassail and treats from the Colonial Dames.
The manor opens to the public in its holiday decorations.
A morning tour of how the mansions are decorated for the holidays.

items.where: West Glocester Fire Station to Ponaganset High School
items.note: Runs east on Route 44 through Chepachet, then Sawmill Road and Snake Hill Road to Ponaganset High School.

items.t: Christmas Open House at the Irish Museum
items.note: The museum’s 10th annual open house, with eggnog and cookies.

items.t: Pictures with Santa and ‘A Visit from St. Nicholas’
items.note: Photos with Santa, with readings of the poem at noon, 12:30 and 1, plus a Spanish-language reading at 1:30.
items.more: RSVP recommended.

items.t: Music in the Living Room at Blithewold
items.note: Holiday music in the decorated manor: mezzo-soprano Nancy Hood on Dec 12 and jazz pianist Laszlo Gardony on Dec 13.
items.price: Ticket includes manor and grounds admission
items.more: Registration required to reserve a seat.

items.t: Holiday Cruises with the Dickens Carolers from Newport
items.note: 75-minute caroling cruises on the Coastal Queen.
items.price: $44 adults; $39 seniors and military; $34 children and youth

items.note: A holiday-season author event.
A seasonal flower-arranging workshop.
The 35th annual bazaar, for the Religious Education Program. Sunday parish breakfast 8–11:45; Santa visits 9:30–12:30.
Crafts, baked goods, raffles, games and food, including the pastor’s pierogis.

items.t: Greek Food Fair and Christmas Bazaar
items.note: Greek food and pastries, coffee, crafts, raffles and a white elephant sale, for the Philoptochos Society’s charity work.
Hot food, baked goods, raffles, a penny social, crafts, knitted goods, wreaths, greenery and a boutique.
items.addr: Parish hall, North Main St., Providence

items.t: St. Vincent de Paul Harvest Bazaar
items.note: Homemade crafts, baked goods, jewelry, a basket raffle, grocery bingo and roll-up tables.
items.addr: 6 St. Vincent de Paul St., Coventry

items.note: Handmade crafts, baked goods, children’s crafts, photos with Santa, raffles, a penny social and a lunch kitchen.
Vendor tables, food, raffles and a silent auction, for the parish food shelf and outreach.

items.t: St. Cecilia Church Hall Christmas Bazaar
items.time: Fri 9 AM–8 PM; Sat 9 AM–2 PM
items.note: Food, raffles, a silent auction, books, crafts, tools, plants and vendors, from St. John Paul II Parish.
items.more: Saturday ticket sales end at 1:30 p.m.

items.note: Bingo, raffles, food, a penny social and caroling by Missy Ducharme Friday from 5 to 6:30.
items.addr: St. Theresa’s Shrine hall, 35 Dion Drive, Nasonville

items.t: St. Francis of Assisi Holiday Bazaar
items.note: Crafters, vendors, a silent auction, bake sale and café, for the parish.
items.addr: Father Greenan Center, 114 High St., Wakefield

items.t: Phillips Memorial Baptist Church Holiday Bazaar
items.note: Handmade gifts, baked goods and family activities.

items.t: St. Martin de Porres Center Holiday Bazaar
items.note: Handmade crafts, home décor, holiday items and gifts. Open to all.

items.t: Seniors’ Christmas Party with Bishop Lewandowski
items.note: Food, fellowship and holiday cheer for seniors. All are welcome.

items.t: Nine Lessons and Carols: Christmas on the Hill
items.note: Trinity Church and its Choir School sing the traditional service of lessons and carols.

items.t: Christmas Lessons and Carols with Choral Holy Eucharist
items.note: The church’s choirs lead this seasonal liturgy.

items.t: Christmas Eve Choral Eucharist with String Quartet
items.note: A festive Eucharist follows prelude music beginning at 9:00 PM.
Families make their own hanukkiah, with PJ Library and Harbor Creative Arts.
items.price: $18 per family, kit included; extra kits $18
items.more: Register by Nov 22.

items.where: Jewish Alliance of Greater Rhode Island
items.note: A Hanukkah shopping pop-up.
items.more: Check the Alliance calendar for place and hours.

sections.label: New Year’s Eve and New Year’s Day

items.t: Noon Year’s Eve at Discovery Lab
items.note: A countdown to noon at the children’s science center.
items.more: Check Discovery Lab for registration and tickets.

items.t: Noon Year’s Eve at Providence Children’s Museum
items.note: Performances, paper crowns and a confetti countdown at noon.
items.more: Confirm this year’s date and tickets with the museum.

items.t: Countdown to Noon Year at MobileQuest
items.note: STEM activities and a countdown for ages 4 to 12 with an adult.
items.more: Preregistration recommended.

items.t: Noon New Year’s Eve Party with the Trolls
items.note: A family skating party, with optional climbing or laser tag.
items.more: Confirm with the rink.

items.t: Noon Year’s Eve at Warwick Public Library
items.note: Dress-up theme, crafts, music, snacks and a countdown to noon.

items.t: Noon Year’s Eve at North Providence Union Free Library
items.note: A craft program and countdown for younger children.
items.more: Registration required; confirm with the library.

items.t: Kids Noon Year’s Eve at Kingston Free Library
items.note: Crafts, games, free play and a balloon drop at noon.
items.more: No food is served.

items.note: Two-hour bowling reservations with lights and music; food available.
items.more: Call the lanes to book.

items.note: The town’s free bonfire, a tradition since 2005: a giant stack of pallets is lit at dusk and families gather around it.

items.t: Providence New Year’s Eve Celebration and Illuminate PVD Fireworks
items.where: 195 District Park and the Van Leesten Pedestrian Bridge
items.note: The city’s free all-ages New Year’s Eve: WaterFire lights the braziers around the bridge at 5:30, SambaViva takes the mainstage at 7, a parade leads into the countdown at 8, and fireworks go up over the Providence River at 8:30.
items.more: Also a DJ and pop-up dancers, roaming performers, food trucks from 5, an after-dark glowing playground with face painting and balloon twisting, a 360 photo booth, an enchanted forest with wishing trees and inflatable sculptures.

items.t: Holiday Lights Spectacular on New Year’s Eve
items.note: More than 3.5 million lights across 40 acres of the zoo.
items.more: Buy tickets online in advance.

items.note: A five- or seven-course seasonal tasting menu, with wine pairings available.
Early seating: a five-course tasting at 5 p.m., $155. Late seating: a ten-course tasting at 8:30, with a midnight countdown and toast, $350.
items.more: Prices are per person before drinks, tax and tip.

items.t: Warwick New Year’s Eve at Rocky Point
items.note: Food trucks, music, giveaways for kids and early fireworks.
items.more: The city hasn’t posted this year’s page yet; confirm with Warwick before going.

items.t: New Year’s Eve Mass in ASL, English and Spanish
items.note: A New Year’s Eve Mass interpreted in American Sign Language, English and Spanish.

items.t: Weekapaug Inn New Year’s Eve Dinner
items.note: A five-course dinner with live music in the Sea Room; wine pairing optional.
A crimson-themed evening: reception, live modern violin, four-course dinner, DJ and dancing, late-night bites and a midnight toast.

items.t: The Dancing Feeling Ballroom New Year’s Eve
items.note: Hors d’oeuvres, buffet, continuous ballroom dancing, a professional American Rhythm show and a midnight toast; dancing until 12:30.

items.t: Little Miss and The Boom at The Blue Room
items.note: Live swing, blues, jazz and rockabilly.
items.more: Ticket and dinner details to come.

items.t: Newport Harbor Island Resort New Year’s Eve
items.note: The Goat Island resort’s New Year’s Eve celebration.
items.more: Entertainment and menu not yet posted.

items.t: Ocean House ‘London Calling’ New Year’s Eve Ball
items.note: A 1960s British-themed ball with a DJ, dancing, food stations, a photo set and costume prizes.
A Chris Stapleton tribute band, dance floor, hats and noisemakers and a midnight toast.
items.more: Doors 7:30.

items.t: Cross’ Mills Library Noon Year’s Eve
items.note: Make hats and noisemakers, play games, sing karaoke, and watch the ball drop at noon.
items.more: Register by phone. Last year it ran 11 to noon; confirm this year’s time.

items.t: A Christmas Carol: New Year’s Eve performance
items.note: The final day of Trinity Rep’s 50th-anniversary Christmas Carol.

items.t: Providence Zen Center New Year’s Eve Practice
items.note: A dinner, evening practice and midnight practice, part of a retreat that begins Dec 30.
items.more: Confirm the Dec 31 schedule and space.

items.note: Hundreds of plungers run into the ocean at noon to raise money for A Wish Come True, which grants wishes to children with life-threatening illnesses.
items.more: Held every New Year’s Day; 2027 details are not posted yet. Parking is limited, so arrive early.
